chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever brings a sacrificial animal for an Umrah, let him slaughter it before he shaves (his head); and whoever brings a sacrificial animal while he is performing Umrah, he slaughters his sacrifice at the slaughter place, which is between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and this is called Al-Hazwara.'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the expiation for the Umrah, where should it be?' So he said: 'In Makkah, unless he delays it to Hajj, in which case it will be in Mina, and hastening it is superior and more beloved to me.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa, one of the hills in Makkah
key_terms.الْحَزْوَرَةُ: Al-Hazwara, the specific area between Safa and Marwa for slaughter
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa, the other hill in Makkah
key_terms.كَفَّارَةِ: Expiation or compensation for a ritual act
key_terms.هَدْياً: Sacrificial animal brought for ritual purposes

ai.seo_question: Where and when should the sacrificial animal be slaughtered during Umrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the procedural nuances of the sacrificial animal (hady) for Umrah, distinguishing between slaughtering before or after shaving the head, and introduces the term 'Al-Hazwara' for the act of slaughtering between Safa and Marwa. It further establishes the preferred location for expiation (kaffarah) as Makkah, while allowing deferral to Mina for those combining Hajj, emphasizing that immediate performance is superior. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise timing and location of ritual acts to maximize spiritual merit.
